content: Internal Revenue Service, Special Investigator Parker speaking. With whom do I have the pleasure of speaking today?
Uh, this is Helen. I got a call saying there was a problem with my taxes?
Yes, Mrs. Helen. According to our IRS records, there are unresolved discrepancies in your recent tax filings. Can you confirm your full name and current mailing address so I can verify your file?
My full name is Helen Ruth Daniels. My address is 742 Willow Avenue, Springfield.
Thank you. I need to confirm your date of birth and the last four digits of your Social Security Number for security purposes.
I was born September 13, 1948, and the last four digits are 2089.

Alright, Helen, I have your case file now. The IRS has detected a serious issue, there is an outstanding balance of $3,670 due to alleged tax evasion from the last two years. Did you intentionally fail to declare any income?
No, no, that can't be right. I just have my Social Security and my pension. I always file everything.

Unfortunately, the system flagged your account for underreporting income, and an arrest warrant has already been processed. If you do not resolve this matter today, your Social Security payments may be suspended and your driver's license revoked.
Oh my goodness, please don't do that! I need those benefits to live. What am I supposed to do?
Helen, I understand this is distressing, but unless you follow precise IRS instructions to settle your account, I am obligated by law to proceed with the arrest warrant and asset seizure.
Please, I can't go to jail. What can I do to fix this?

Because you contacted us promptly, you are eligible to resolve this outside of court. You must make an immediate payment of at least $1,850 today to halt the legal process and stop the suspension of your benefits.
I don't have that kind of money. I just have a little in my checking account.
How much do you have available right now, Helen? List the amounts in your checking, savings, and on any credit cards.
I think maybe $600 in checking, and about $400 on my Visa card.

That will suffice for today as a partial payment. For security reasons, IRS policy requires this to be paid via instant transfer. Do you have access to Zelle or Cash App, or do you prefer to make the payment using gift cards?
Um, I have Cash App, but I'm not sure how it works. I've never done this before.
No problem. I will guide you step by step. First, open your Cash App and let me know when you're ready. I'll provide you with the IRS payment handle.
Okay, I have it open. What do I do?
Enter $1,000 and send it to $IRSProcessingDept. Once you've done that, confirm the transaction ID for our records.
Alright, I think I sent it. The app says the ID is TX982735.

Thank you, Helen. I see the payment here. Now, for the remaining balance, you will need to purchase four Walmart gift cards of $200 each. Go to your nearest store, buy the cards, and call me back with the codes. This must be done within the next hour to stop further action.
I don't drive much anymore. Is there any other way I can pay?
I understand, but IRS protocol requires gift card verification for immediate payments. If you are unable to comply, the arrest process cannot be paused. Do you wish to proceed?
Okay, okay, I'll try to get someone to take me. Please don't do anything until I call back.

That's acceptable, Helen. I am placing your file on a temporary hold for 60 minutes. Remember, if you fail to call back with the gift card codes, your Social Security will be frozen and your case will be escalated to law enforcement. Is that clear?
Yes, yes, I understand. I'll call back as soon as I get the cards.
